Rashi on Ketubot 15a:11:1.hebrew: אלא מתשעה צפרדעים כו' - תוספתא היא במס' טהרות: תשעה צפרדעים מתים ברשות היחיד, ושרץ אחד — כגון צב, שהוא דומה לצפרדע — ביניהם, ונגע באחד מהן, ספיקו טמא:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:11:1.english: Rather, from nine frogs, etc. - It is a Tosefta in Tractate Tahorot: Nine dead frogs in a private domain, and one creeping animal — such as a toad, which resembles a frog — [is] among them, and [someone] touched one of them, its uncertain [case] is ritually impure.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:12:1.hebrew: אלא מתשעה שרצים כו' - אף היא תוספתא במס' טהרות, וקתני: ברה"י ספיקו טמא, ברה"ר ספיקו טהור. אלמא כמחצה דמי ולקולא; דאי לאו כמחצה דמי, אין כאן ספק טומאה אלא ודאי טומאה, דהא רובא שרצים:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:12:1.english: Rather, from nine creeping animals, etc. - This too is a Tosefta in Tractate Tohorot, and it teaches: in a private domain its uncertainty is [ruled] impure, [and] in a public domain its uncertainty is [ruled] pure. Thus, it is regarded as half-and-half, and [this is] for leniency; for if it were not regarded as half-and-half, there would be no uncertainty of impurity here, but rather definite impurity, since the majority are creeping animals.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:13:1.hebrew: אמר קרא וארב לו עד שיהא מתכוין לו - פרט למתכוין להרוג את זה והרג את זה. הכי דריש ליה ר"ש בסנהדרין, ואמרינן התם: ורבנן היכי דרשי ליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:13:1.english: The verse states: "And lie in wait for him" — until he intends [to kill] him - Excluding one who intends to kill this [person] and kills that [person]. Thus Rabbi Shimon expounds it in Sanhedrin, and we say there: "And how do the Rabbis expound it?"

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:13:2.hebrew: אמרי דבי ר' ינאי פרט לזורק אבן לגו - לתוך חבורת בני אדם, כנענים וישראלים. אבל שני ישראלים עומדין, ונתכוין להרוג זה (והרג זה), והתרו בו וקבל התראה, ונפלה הכאה על חבירו — חייב. והיינו טעמא דקאמר הכא "ורבנן", משום דבסנהדרין הכי איתא:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:13:2.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai say: [It] excludes one who throws a stone into [a crowd] - Into a group of people, Canaanites and Israelites. However, [if] two Israelites are standing [there], and he intended to kill this one (and killed that one), and they warned him and he accepted the warning, and the blow fell upon his fellow — he is liable. And this is the reason that [the Gemara] says here, "And the Rabbis," because in Sanhedrin it is stated thus.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:14:1.hebrew: תיפוק ליה דרובא כנענים נינהו - ולמה לי קרא? ואי נמי פלגא ופלגא, אכתי לא איצטריך קרא, דמהיכא תיתי דניקטליה:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:14:1.english: Let it be derived that the majority are Canaanites - And why do I need a verse? And even if [it is] half and half, still a verse is not needed, for from where would it enter [one's mind] that we should execute him?

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:14:2.hebrew: ספק נפשות - דיני נפשות להקל, דהא "והצילו העדה" כתיב (במדבר ל״ה:כ״ה):
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:14:2.english: Uncertainty [concerning] lives - Capital cases [are ruled] leniently, for behold, it is written, "And the congregation shall rescue" (Numbers 35:25).

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:15:1.english: Since the gentile is fixed among them - And this verse teaches us that anything fixed is like half-and-half.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:16:1.hebrew: הוראת שעה היתה - הך דריב"נ צורך שעה היתה, או ראו שם שאר צידי היכר דברים להתיר, אבל לדורות תרי רובי בעינן:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:16:1.english: It was a provisional edict - That [case] of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri was an exigency of the hour, or they saw there other indicative circumstances to permit [her], but for [future] generations, we require two majorities.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:17:1.hebrew: מתיב רבי ירמיה כו' - קס"ד דמשום רוב העיר גרידתא אכשרוה, ואמר רב הלכה כרבי יוסי:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:17:1.english: Rabbi Yirmeya raised an objection, etc. - He initially assumed that [the Sages] declared her fit solely because of the majority of the city, and [that] Rav said the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:1:1.hebrew: בקרונות של ציפורי - ביום השוק, שסיעות ושיירות ממקום אחר באות שם:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:1:1.english: Among the wagons of Tzippori - On the market day, when groups and caravans from another place come there.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:1:2.english: And in accordance with Rabbi Ami - For now there is a majority of the contingent and a majority of the city [that are of unflawed lineage].

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:1:3.english: One who engaged in intercourse in the wagons - [This] implies on the wagon.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:2:1.english: At the time of the wagons - When the caravans come to the city.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:2:2.hebrew: כשרה לכהונה - כדקאמר, והוא שהיתה סיעה של בני אדם כשרים עוברת שם, דאיכא למימר שמהם היה:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:2:2.english: [She is] fit for the priesthood - As he states: [this applies] provided that a group of fit men was passing there, for one can say that he was from them.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:2:3.hebrew: אבל פירש אחד מציפורי - דידעינן ודאי דמן העיר היה, אע"פ שציפורי עיר שרובה משיאין לכהונה:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:2:3.english: However, [if] one left Tzippori - Where we know with certainty that he was from the city, even though Tzippori is a city whose majority [of inhabitants] marry into the priesthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:2:4.english: The child is a shetuki - For with a single majority, [the child] is not deemed fit.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:3:1.hebrew: וכי הא דכי אתא רב דימי אמר זעירי אמר רבי חנינא ואמרי לה - שלא הוזכר רב דימי כאן, אלא זעירי אמר רבי חנינא, דבעינן תרי רובי, וכדמפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:3:1.english: And like this [statement], that when Rav Dimi came, Ze'eiri said [that] Rabbi Chanina said, and some say - That Rav Dimi was not mentioned here; rather, Ze'eiri said [that] Rabbi Chanina said that we require two majorities, and as [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:3:2.english: One follows the majority of the city - to render [her] fit [for the priesthood].

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:3:3.hebrew: ואין הולכין אחר רוב סיעה - כגון במקום רחוק מן העיר, דבודאי מאנשי הסיעה הוה, אין מכשירין אותה, ואפילו רובן כשרין:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:3:3.english: And one does not follow the majority of a contingent - For example, in a place far from the city, where [the man] was certainly from the members of the contingent, we do not declare her fit [to marry into the priesthood], even if the majority of them are of fit [lineage].

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:4:1.english: And we have a difficulty: kelapei layya - Toward where does this matter turn?

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:4:2.hebrew: הני ניידי - רוב סיעה ניידי, ויש להלך בהן אחר הרוב:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:4:2.english: These are moving - The majority of the contingent are moving, and one follows the majority regarding them.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:4:4.hebrew: קביעי - ואמרינן לקמן: כל קבוע כמחצה על מחצה דמי, ואפילו אין שם אלא אחד, פסולה:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:4:4.english: [They are] fixed - And we say later [in the Gemara]: every fixed [case] is [considered] like half and half, and even if there is only one [disqualified person] there, she is disqualified.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:5:1.hebrew: ולא אחר רוב סיעה גרידתא - והכי קאמר: אין הולכין אחר רוב סיעה לבדה, וכל שכן אחר רוב העיר לבדה:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:5:1.english: Nor [does one follow] the majority of the contingent alone - And this is what it is saying: one does not follow the majority of the contingent by itself, and all the more so [not] the majority of the city by itself.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:5:2.hebrew: מ"ט - אחר רוב סיעה לא:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:5:2.english: What is the reason - [that one does] not [follow] the majority of the contingent?

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:5:3.english: A decree due to the majority of the city - Because they are fixed [in place].

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:6:1.hebrew: ופרכינן: רוב העיר נמי, אי עקר הבועל מביתו ואזל לגבה — הוה נייד, <abbr title="וקיימא לן">וקי"ל</abbr> כל דפריש מרובא פריש:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:6:1.english: And we ask: [Regarding] the majority of the city as well — if the man who had intercourse with her moved from his house and went to her, he is mobile, and we hold [that] anything that separates [from a group] separates from the majority.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:6:2.hebrew: ומשני: איכא דקאזלא לגבייהו כו' — ולא גרסינן מאי איכא — יש שהולכת היא אצלו והוה ליה קבוע. הלכך, אפילו ברוב כשרים — או רוב העיר או רוב סיעה — פסול כרבי יהושע, ומשום תרי רובי אכשרה, דליכא למיגזר מידי:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:6:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: "There is [a case] where she goes to them, etc." — and we do not read "what is there [to say]?" — [meaning] there are [times] when she goes to him, and it is [considered] fixed [in its place]. Therefore, even with a majority of fit [men] — whether the majority of the city or the majority of a caravan — [it is] disqualified, in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua, and it is because of two majorities that [Rabban Gamliel] declared her fit, for there is nothing to decree.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:7:1.english: And he bought meat from one of them - In a fixed place.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:7:2.english: Its uncertainty is prohibited - For anything fixed [in its place] is like half and half.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:7:3.english: And in [the case of meat] found - Meat that is found in the market, and we do not know from which [store] it separated.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:7:4.hebrew: הלך אחר הרוב - הואיל והבא לפנינו לא במקום קביעות לקחה, וכבר פירשה על ידי אחר, וכל דפריש מרובא פריש:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:7:4.english: Follow the majority - Since the one who comes before us did not take it in a fixed place, and it already separated through another [person], and anything that separates, separates from the majority.

Rashi on Ketubot 15a:8:1.hebrew: דקאתי לה רובא מעלמא - וכגון שרוב סיעת טבחי ישראל כשרים באו לכאן, דאיכא תרי רובי, או שרוב טבחי כל המדינה ישראל, דאיכא תרי רובי — רוב העיר ורוב המדינה דניידי:
Rashi on Ketubot 15a:8:1.english: Where the majority comes to it from outside - And [this is] a case where the majority of a group of kosher Jewish butchers came here, so that there are two majorities, or where the majority of the butchers of the entire province are Jewish, so that there are two majorities — the majority of the city and the majority of the province, who are mobile.

Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:13:1.hebrew: פרט לזורק אבן לגו - תימה, דלר' שמעון קבוע מנא ליה? ואין לומר דמסקינן בפ' הנשרפין (סנהדרין דף עט. ושם) דר"ש סבר כרבי, דיליף "נתינה" "נתינה", ואייתר ליה "וארב לו" לקבוע — דאכתי, לתנא דבי חזקיה מנא ליה קבוע? דלית ליה דרבי, דהא באין מתכוין פטור מממון:
Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:13:1.english: "Except for one who throws a stone into a crowd" - It is astonishing: according to Rabbi Shimon, from where does he [derive the law of] kavu'a [a fixed item]? And one cannot say that [this is resolved because] we conclude in the chapter [entitled] HaNisrafin (Sanhedrin 79a and there) that Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi [Yehudah HaNasi], who derives [the exemption for unintentional killing from] "giving" [and] "giving," and thus "and lie in wait for him" is left over for him [to teach] kavu'a — for still, according to the Tanna of the school of Chizkiyah, from where does he [derive] kavu'a? For he does not hold of Rabbi's [derivation], since in [a case of] unintentional [killing] he is exempt from monetary payment [as well].

Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:14:1.hebrew: וספק נפשות להקל - תימה: למ"ד התראת ספק לא שמה התראה, אפילו ספק נפשות להחמיר פטור, משום דהתראת ספק היא; ואי למ"ד שמה התראה, היכי פטרינן ליה כשנמצא שישראל הרג? הא מיחייב ב"הכה את זה וחזר והכה את זה", ובנותר כשאמרו לו "אל תותיר", אע"ג דספק הוא. וי"ל דשאני התם, שיודע בודאי שיבא לידי איסור אם יותיר או יכה שניהם, מש"ה שמה התראה; אבל הכא אינו יודע שודאי יבוא לידי איסור, שאינו יודע את מי יכה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:14:1.english: And uncertainty in capital cases is [judged] leniently - This is astonishing: according to the one who says [that] an uncertain warning is not considered a [valid] warning, even [if the rule were that] uncertainty in capital cases is [judged] stringently, he would be exempt because it is an uncertain warning. And if [we follow] the one who says [that it] is considered a [valid] warning, how do we exempt him when it is found that he killed a Jew? Behold, he is liable in [the case of] "he struck this one and then struck that one," and in [the case of] notar [leftover sacrificial meat] when they said to him, "Do not leave [any] over," even though it is uncertain. And one can answer that there it is different, because he knows with certainty that he will come to a prohibition if he leaves [meat] over or strikes both of them; therefore it is considered a [valid] warning. But here, he does not know that he will certainly come to a prohibition, for he does not know whom he will strike.

Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:17:1.hebrew: וליוחסין לא בעינן תרי רובי ורמינהי כו' - הוה מצי לשנויי שאני תינוק, דלית לי' חזק' דכשרו':
Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:17:1.english: "And in matters of lineage, do we not require two majorities? And [yet] we raise a contradiction, etc." - [The Gemara] could have answered [that] a [foundling] child is different, since he does not have a presumptive status of fitness.

Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:6:1.hebrew: דלמא אזלא איהי לגבייהו - פי': לתוך ביתם, דאפילו בתוך העיר לא חשיב קבוע, דדמי לנמצא בין החנויות דלא חשיב קבוע; וכן גבי תינוק מושלך בעיר לא חשיב קבוע, הואיל ולא נמצא בבית. ולכך פירש בקונטרס שפירש בועל מביתו. וא"ת: דבנזיר פ"ב (דף יב. ושם) פריך אהא דאמר: "האומר לשלוחו: צא וקדש לי אשה סתם, אסור בכל הנשים שבעולם" — מקן סתומה, ומסיק: "אמינא לך אנא אשה דלא ניידא, ואת אמרת לי איסורא דנייד? וכי תימא: ה"נ בשוקא אשכחה וקדיש — התם הדרא לניחותא!" משמע: לגבי אדם לא שייך "כל דפריש מרובא פריש", משום דהדר לניחותיה! ולאו פירכא היא: דהתם בשעת האיסור — כשזה בא על שום אשה — הדרא לניחותא האשה שקידש השליח; אבל הכא, כי אזלי אינהו לגבה, בשעה שאוסרה הרי הוא נייד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 15a:6:1.english: Perhaps she went to them - This means: into their house; for even within the city [if she met him in the street], it is not considered a fixed [set], as it is similar to [meat] found among the shops, which is not considered fixed. Similarly, regarding an abandoned child [found] in a city, it is not considered fixed since he was not found in a house. And therefore Rashi explained [earlier] that the man [who had intercourse with her] separated from his house. And if you will say: In Nazir, chapter 2 (12a and thereabouts), [the Gemara] raises an objection against that which was stated: "One who says to his agent, 'Go and betroth for me an unspecified woman,' is forbidden to all women in the world" — from [the case of] an unspecified bird-nest offering; and [the Gemara] concludes: "I am speaking to you of a woman, who does not move about, and you are citing to me a prohibition [i.e., a bird] that moves about! And if you would say that here too, [the agent] found her in the marketplace and betrothed her [while she was moving about] — there, she returns to her resting place!" This implies that with respect to a person, [the principle of] "anything that separates, separates from the majority" does not apply, because [a person] returns to his resting place! But this is not a difficulty: for there, at the time of the prohibition — when this [man] has intercourse with any woman — the woman whom the agent betrothed has [already] returned to her resting place; whereas here, when they go out to her, at the time he renders her forbidden [by having intercourse with her], he is moving about.
